note: Shared by Go validateFindingBulk (internal/app/finding_bulk_due_test.go) and TS findingBulkPatch (web/tests/finding-bulk.test.mjs). The two readers do NOT see the same string: "form.due" is the browser-local value a datetime-local control holds, and "wire" is the string findingBulkPatch puts into patch.due_date and therefore the only string the server ever judges, because the form submits new Date(due).toISOString(). The conversion is browser-time-zone dependent, so "form.tz" is part of the input: the same typed value 9999-12-31T23:59 stays a four digit year east of UTC and overflows into the extended year +010000 west of it. "accepted" is the single verdict both sides must reach, decided by validateFindingOpsResource (internal/app/finding_ops.go), which parses with time.Parse(time.RFC3339, s) and so takes exactly four year digits with no sign. ECMA-262 Date.prototype.toISOString emits the expanded year form (+YYYYYY / -YYYYYY) outside 0000-9999, which that layout cannot read, and internal/app/finding_bulk.go turns the error into findingBulkError{400} that rolls back the whole request including the assignee and status in the same patch. So the form must throw instead of submitting any wire string marked accepted:false. Year 0000 is accepted on both sides: the server cares about the four digit shape, not about the year being at least 1. A datetime-local control cannot produce the year-0000 inputs below (HTML requires a year greater than zero), so those rows pin the function contract rather than a proven browser path; the year-9999 rows are an ordinary typeable value and are the reachable failure.
